name: Shelah
title: Judas third son
summary: Shelah was the third son of Judah and his Canaanite wife, Bath-Shua. He was promised as a husband to Tamar after his two older brothers Er and Onan died, but Judah did not keep his promise. Shelah became the ancestor of a clan within the tribe of Judah, and his descendants are mentioned in several genealogies in the Old Testament.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Shelah
keyEvents.description: Shelah was born in Chezib as the third son of Judah and his Canaanite wife Bath-Shua.

keyEvents.title: Tamar Promised to Shelah
keyEvents.description: After Onan's death, Judah promised Tamar that she would have Shelah as her husband when he grew up, but Judah feared that Shelah might also die.

keyEvents.title: Judah Breaks His Promise Regarding Shelah
keyEvents.description: Tamar realized that Shelah had grown up without Judah fulfilling his promise to give him to her as a wife, which led her to take matters into her own hands.

keyEvents.title: Shelah in the Genealogy of Genesis
keyEvents.description: Shelah is mentioned as one of Judah's sons who went down to Egypt with Jacob and his family.

keyEvents.title: The Lineage of the Shelanites in the Census
keyEvents.description: In the census in the wilderness, Shelah's descendants, the Shelanites, were counted among the clans of the tribe of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Shelah's Descendants in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: First Chronicles gives a detailed overview of Shelah's descendants, including craftsmen and rulers who settled in various cities in Judah.
